summary: Discovery call focused on Redwood PLG quickstart, free credits, and evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for Sylpha's analytics inference needs. Primary concerns: time-to-first-token, data residency, latency/cost tradeoffs, and path to production (pilot -> dedicated). AE to send quickstart and credits; SE to run benchmark plan.
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: 45 min
- Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CTO, Sylpha), Ethan Huang (ML Eng, Sylpha), Jill Romero (Head of Eng, Sylpha)

Summary: quick discovery, fairly PLG-focused team, want to validate quickstart and run simple benchmark. They have internal infra constraints around PII and want to understand path to dedicated / private if pilot looks good.

[00:00] Samantha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm sam from redwood, quick intros?
[00:08] Maya: maya here, cto at sylpha, we run analytics pipelines and want to add lightweight llm features to our ui, mostly summarization and reranking today
[00:18] Ethan: hey, ethan, ml eng, i'll be hands on for the trial and benchmarks
[00:23] Jill: jill, ops/eng lead, i'll be watching infra/security needs
[00:28] Diego: diego from redwood, i'll cover perf and infra options, thanks

[01:05] Samantha: great, high level, redwood has a plg quickstart api, free credits, should be able to get you first token in minutes, question for you - what are your primary success criteria for a pilot?
[01:20] Maya: we want to measure latency under our UI constraints (95th pctl < 400ms ideally), and cost per thousand tokens, and obviously no data leakage - we have customer pII in some docs, so residency / retention is important
[01:38] Ethan: also want to see integration speed - dev onramps, sample code, sdk, time-to-first-token is a big deal for our PMs

[02:10] Samantha: noted. quickstart typically: sign up, create api key, use sample curl or sdk, we give credits, can hit hosted endpoints right away. time-to-first-token often sub-10 minutes for devs. if you need dedicated capacity we can provision, but that's usually later after pilot
[02:38] Jill: on dedicated vs hosted, our security team will want control over logs/audit and possibly a private vpc. what are the controls on hosted for retention and audit logs?
[02:52] Diego: for hosted we have configurable retention windows and we log request traces in console; we also support customer-managed kms for dedicated/private and audit log export. hosted is multi-tenant but with strong isolation and soc2 compliance; private gives you the control if regs require it

[04:05] Maya: do you have examples of customers moving from plg hosted pilot to dedicated? what's the usual timeline and blockers?
[04:16] Samantha: yes, many orgs start hosted to iterate fast, then commit to dedicated when they need throughput SLAs or want cost predictability. timeline depends on procurement but technically can be days to weeks for dedicated capacity, meanwhile private deployments take longer because of networking and certs, often 6-8 weeks for on-prem or vpc setups

[06:00] Ethan: about perf - do you have a benchmarking kit? we need to compare open models and quantized variants and see cost/latency tradeoffs
[06:12] Diego: we do; i'll share a perf plan that runs tokens/sec, p50/p95 p99, memory/KV behaviour. for quickstart you can run hosted with a sample model in our catalog and i'll include recommended model/quantization suggestions for conversational/summarization workloads

[08:30] Maya: what's the smallest effort to get something on staging? can devs do a curl from laptop to hosted and test with sample data?
[08:40] Samantha: absolutely. steps: sign up, get api key, run sample curl, try sdk snippet, verify response streaming; we'll send you a quickstart doc and a ready-to-run notebook. free credits are applied to your account so you can run tests without billing concerns

[10:05] Jill: any rate limits or throttles that might bite during our load tests? we expect spikes from UI batch summarization
[10:18] Diego: hosted has default rate limits but we can lift for trial or recommend batching and concurrency settings. dedicated gives predictable throughput; you can configure autoscaling and burst capacity if needed

[12:00] Ethan: question on data: if we pass customer documents that include pII to hosted, how is that handled? do you retain payloads? can we opt out of logging?
[12:15] Diego: hosted by default retains logs for a configurable window, but you can request minimal retention for sensitive workloads; for complete control, dedicated/private with customer-managed kms and no-logs options is the route. we also support data deletion requests and have SOC 2/ISO compliance artifacts

[14:20] Maya: ok, procurement will ask about encryption; do you integrate with AWS KMS / HSM?
[14:28] Samantha: yes, for private and dedicated we support customer-managed keys (aws kms, gcp kms) and HSM integrations on request. we'll include security pack and SOC2 report in the followup

[16:05] Jill: i want to understand pricing signals - hosted per-token, dedicated reserved capacity? how do we compare cost for our expected throughput?
[16:18] Samantha: hosted is usage-based per token/embedding; dedicated is reserved monthly with unit economics for tokens/sec; i'll include a sample cost sheet. Diego will help estimate for your workload after you share traffic profile

[18:40] Ethan: for the quickstart, do we need to sign anything? can we use feature flags and iterate without a contract?
[18:50] Samantha: quickstart is self-serve, free credits let you test without procurement. if you need enterprise SLAs we move to a contract for dedicated/private

[21:00] Maya: any gotchas about model compatibility with our inference code? we use an LLM pipeline that expects streaming and tool-calling support
[21:12] Diego: redwood runtime supports streaming, function/tool calling, and modern kv cache patterns. some names get garbled in transcripts but to be clear, we support streaming tokens, structured outputs, and can route to compatible model variants if cost/latency needs change

[24:30] Samantha: ok let's talk timeline and next steps - what do you want to see in the pilot?
[24:45] Maya: 1) dev time-to-first-token verified, 2) perf benchmark for our sample dataset, p95 under 400ms target, 3) cost estimate for 100k tokens/day, 4) security docs for hosted retention and path to dedicated/private

[25:20] Samantha: perfect, we'll deliver that. diego will own the perf plan; i'll send quickstart and credits; ethan will share dataset and target sros - sorry slos.
[25:42] Ethan: will do, i'll get a sanitized subset this week

[27:10] Jill: procurement will likely want to see SOC2, SSO/SAML, and data processing addendum - any standard templates?
[27:22] Samantha: yes, we have standard DPA and SSO integrations; we'll attach those in the followup email along with SOC2 report and security FAQ

[30:00] Diego: quick note on metrics - for summarization models p95 numbers depend a lot on sequence length and kv cache behaviour, i'll include a matrix with recommended model family and quantization levels to meet your p95 goals while controlling cost

[33:05] Maya: any competitors you see in this space that we should consider?
[33:12] Samantha: common comparisons are openai for hosted simplicity, anthropic for safety models, and cloud vendors like sage maker for self-hosted managed endpoints; we'll try and highlight where redwood gives dev velocity plus an easy path to dedicated/private

[35:40] Ethan: what's the easiest way to collaborate on the trial? do you provision a workspace or repo we can access?
[35:50] Samantha: we can spin up a trial org in the console and invite your emails, or share a repo/notebook. i'll provision a trial workspace and invite ethan and maya after the call

[38:10] Jill: any limits on bringing your own models? we might want to test a quantized open model on dedicated infra
[38:20] Diego: yes, we onboard customer models; dedicated/private work better for BYOM (bring your own model) due to licensing and kernel selection needs. we'll include model onboarding notes in the perf plan

[40:00] Samantha: recap quickly - action items: sam to send quickstart + credits + security docs; diego to send perf/benchmark plan and cost estimate; ethan to share dataset and slos; schedule follow-up demo/benchmark week of 2026-03-15. any other items?
[40:20] Maya: sounds good, thanks
[40:25] Ethan: thanks all
[40:30] Jill: thanks

[41:00] Samantha: we'll follow up with a single email that includes the quickstart, steps for time-to-first-token, and a proposed benchmark schedule
[41:10] Diego: i'll include a checklist for hosted vs dedicated decisions and a simple cost worksheet
[42:00] Meeting end

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (sros/slos), some proper nouns transcribed inconsistently, speaker turns approximated.
questions: How quickly can Sylpha get time-to-first-token with hosted quickstart?
What are the retention/logging options for hosted vs dedicated?
What's the expected timeline and blockers for moving from hosted pilot to dedicated/private?
